api_proxy_type.description:
Optional. API Proxy type supported by the environment. The type can be set when creating
the Environment and cannot be changed. Possible values: ["API_PROXY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "PROGRAMMABLE", "CONFIGURABLE"]
api_proxy_type.rationale: api_proxy_type is an architectural constraint that defines the execution model of API proxies. It does not control access permissions, encryption, network exposure, or any CIA security threat within the Apigee platform.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

deployment_type.description:
Optional. Deployment type supported by the environment. The deployment type can be
set when creating the environment and cannot be changed. When you enable archive
deployment, you will be prevented from performing a subset of actions within the
environment, including:
Managing the deployment of API proxy or shared flow revisions;
Creating, updating, or deleting resource files;
Creating, updating, or deleting target servers. Possible values: ["DEPLOYMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "PROXY", "ARCHIVE"]
deployment_type.rationale: deployment_type defines how API proxies are deployed in the environment. The risk is unpredictability not exposure, data leakage or privilege escalation, so it is not a security concern.

description.rationale: It sets the description only and does not have any security impact.

display_name.rationale: It sets the display name only and does not have any security impact.

forward_proxy_uri.description: Optional. URI of the forward proxy to be applied to the runtime instances in this environment. Must be in the format of {scheme}://{hostname}:{port}. Note that the scheme must be one of "http" or "https", and the port must be supplied.
forward_proxy_uri.rationale: Using insecure schemes such as ftp, ssh, or telnet for the forward proxy exposes API traffic to interception and man-in-the-middle attacks. Only http:// or https:// schemes should be used.

name.description: The resource ID of the environment.
name.rationale: It sets the name of the environment and does not have any security impact.

org_id.description:
The Apigee Organization associated with the Apigee environment,
in the format 'organizations/{{org_name}}'.
org_id.rationale: It sets the organization association and does not have any direct security impact.

type.description:
Types that can be selected for an Environment. Each of the types are
limited by capability and capacity. Refer to Apigee's public documentation
to understand about each of these types in details.
An Apigee org can support heterogeneous Environments. Possible values: ["ENVIRONMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "BASE", "INTERMEDIATE", "COMPREHENSIVE"]
type.rationale: type defines the feature set and scale tier available to the environment. It controls performance capabilities not security mechanisms such as access control or encryption.

client_ip_resolution_config.description: The algorithm to resolve IP. This will affect Analytics, API Security, and other features that use the client ip. To remove a client ip resolution config, update the field to an empty value. Example: '{ "clientIpResolutionConfig" = {} }' For more information, see: https://cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/system-administration/client-ip-resolution

client_ip_resolution_config.header_index.description: Resolves the client ip based on a custom header.
The index of the ip in the header. Positive indices 0, 1, 2, 3 chooses indices from the left (first ips). Negative indices -1, -2, -3 chooses indices from the right (last ips).
client_ip_resolution_config.header_index.rationale: Using a non-negative index (0, 1, 2...) reads client-supplied IPs from the X-Forwarded-For header, which can be spoofed by malicious clients. Setting ip_header_index to -1 ensures the last verified hop is used, which cannot be spoofed.

client_ip_resolution_config.header_index.description: The name of the header to extract the client ip from. We are currently only supporting the X-Forwarded-For header.
client_ip_resolution_config.header_index.rationale: It sets the header name for IP extraction. Only X-Forwarded-For is currently supported and does not have additional security impact.

node_config.description: NodeConfig for setting the min/max number of nodes associated with the environment.

node_config.max_node_count.description:
The maximum total number of gateway nodes that the is reserved for all instances that
has the specified environment. If not specified, the default is determined by the
recommended maximum number of nodes for that gateway.
node_config.max_node_count.rationale: It sets the maximum node count for scaling and does not have any security impact.

node_config.min_node_count.description:
The minimum total number of gateway nodes that the is reserved for all instances that
has the specified environment. If not specified, the default is determined by the
recommended minimum number of nodes for that gateway.
node_config.min_node_count.rationale: It sets the minimum node count for scaling and does not have any security impact.

properties.description: Key-value pairs that may be used for customizing the environment.

properties.property.description: List of all properties in the object.
